title: Brand Kit
description: Brand identity, voice, and reusable guidance for every piece of content.
voiceDescription: The tone, do's, and don'ts every planner and reviewer should follow. The rules surface in the editor's draft-time hints.
colorsDescription: Primary, secondary, accent, and neutral hexes. Designers and copywriters grab the hex with one click.
publishingDescription: Editorial guardrails — alt text conventions, hashtag norms, compliance reminders, per-channel guidance.
logosDescription: The primary mark, secondary marks, and reference logos that every designer, planner, and reviewer should ship in.
activityDescription: The latest changes to the brand kit — assets, voice rules, publishing rules, and linked resources. As the team edits, the feed updates here.
pillarsDescription: The recurring topics every plan and post should align to. The AI uses pillar names + blurbs as context for caption drafts.
linkedDescription: The Figma, Drive, Canva, and Dropbox libraries the team uses to source on-brand material.
typographyDescription: The headline, body, accent, and mono faces that every asset should ship in. Each entry renders a live sample.
templatesDescription: Curated seeds for every section of your brand kit. Pick what fits and one-click add — your brand kit grows without you having to write every rule from scratch.
templatesSectionVoiceBlurb: Tone, do, and don't rule seeds. The AI uses the voice rules you keep as the strongest signal in caption drafts.
templatesSectionPillarsBlurb: Content pillar seeds to bootstrap the taxonomy. Each pillar carries a one-sentence description the AI uses to keep caption drafts on-topic.
templatesSectionPalettesBlurb: Five-color starter palettes with role assignments. Each click adds every swatch that isn't already in your palette.
templatesSectionTypographyBlurb: Headline + body face pairings. Each click adds every face in the pair that isn't already catalogued.
templatesSectionPublishingBlurb: Editorial guardrails for the team. Each click adds the rule to your publishing rules list.

empty.logosDescription: Upload a PNG, JPG, or SVG — or paste an external URL — so every planner, designer, and reviewer has the same starting point.
empty.colorsDescription: Add the brand's primary, secondary, and accent hexes. Designers and copywriters can grab the hex with one click.
empty.typographyDescription: Document the headline, body, and accent faces so designers ship in one voice. Each entry gets a live sample.
empty.voiceDescription: Add do/don't/tone rules so the team writes in one voice. The rules surface in the editor's draft-time hints.
empty.pillarsDescription: Pillars are the recurring topics every plan and post should align to. The AI uses pillar names + blurbs as context for caption drafts.
empty.publishingDescription: Add the first one to set editorial guardrails — alt text, hashtag norms, compliance reminders — for the team.
empty.linkedDescription: Link a Google Drive, Figma, Canva, or Dropbox library so the team knows where to source on-brand material.
empty.recentDescription: As the team adds logos, colors, fonts, voice rules, and publishing guidelines, the latest changes will appear here.

overview.downloadZipEmpty: Add at least one logo, color, or font before downloading.

aiDescription.logos: Not fed to the AI. Logos are visual brand-mark context reserved for a future image-generation capability.
aiDescription.colors: Fed to the AI when the Brand Visuals toggle is on. Color names, hex values, and roles surface in caption drafts so the model can recommend on-brand palettes.
aiDescription.typography: Fed to the AI when the Brand Visuals toggle is on. Font families, weights, and roles help the model reference the workspace's type system.
aiDescription.voice: Fed to the AI right now. Tone, do, and don't rules surface in caption drafts and brief improvements.
aiDescription.pillars: Fed to the AI right now. Pillar names and blurbs keep caption drafts on-topic.
aiDescription.publishing: Fed to the AI when the Brand Visuals toggle is on. Alt-text, hashtag, and compliance rules are appended to the prompt so the AI follows editorial guardrails.
aiDescription.linked: Not fed to the AI by design. Linked resources are for the human team; the activity feed also strips their URLs for viewer privacy.

suggestions.logosEmpty: Add your first logo so designers have a single source for the brand mark.
suggestions.logosOne: Add 2–3 variants (light, dark, monochrome) so designers can pick the right mark for each surface.
suggestions.logosThin: Solid coverage. Consider an icon-only mark for small surfaces (favicons, app icons, avatars).
suggestions.colorsEmpty: Add a Primary colour first. The AI uses it as the default recommendation in caption drafts.
suggestions.colorsMissingRoles: Mark a role for each color (Primary / Secondary / Accent / Neutral) so the AI can group recommendations.
suggestions.colorsMissingSome: Add {roles} color to round out the palette — the AI leans on these in caption drafts.
suggestions.colorsVariants: Solid 4-role palette. Consider 1–2 more variants of each role for dark-mode and high-contrast use.
suggestions.colorsHealthy: Healthy palette with full role coverage.
suggestions.typographyEmpty: Add a headline + body font. Brand Visuals is on; the AI now uses these in caption drafts.
suggestions.typographyHeadline: Add a Headline face first — it sets the tone for the entire type system.
suggestions.typographyBody: Add a Body face to pair with your Headline so the type system has a hierarchy.
suggestions.typographyAccent: Solid pair. Add an Accent or Mono face if you need emphasis or code-style content.
suggestions.voiceEmpty: Add at least 1 tone rule + 2 do rules + 1 don't rule. The AI mirrors all three.
suggestions.voiceTone: Add a tone rule. The AI uses tone as the single strongest voice signal in drafts.
suggestions.voiceDo: Add 2–3 do rules. The AI mirrors them as positive patterns.
suggestions.voiceDont: Add 1–2 don't rules. Without them, the AI has no way to avoid the patterns you don't want.
suggestions.pillarsEmpty: Add 3–5 pillars. The AI uses pillar names + blurbs to keep caption drafts on-topic.
suggestions.pillarsThin: Most agencies benefit from 3–5 pillars. Two is a thin basis for AI to lean on.
suggestions.pillarsMany: Six or more can dilute focus. Consider consolidating the least-active pillars.
suggestions.publishingEmpty: Add 1–2 alt-text rules + 1–2 hashtag norms. Brand Visuals is on; the AI uses these in drafts.
suggestions.publishingThin: Add at least one compliance + one channel-specific rule for full editorial coverage.
suggestions.linkedEmpty: Link a Figma or Drive library so the team has one place to find on-brand material.
suggestions.linkedOne: Healthy. Add a second library (e.g. Canva + Figma) for cross-tool teams.
suggestions.linkedHealthy: Healthy. Linked resources are intentionally not fed to the AI — they stay for the human team.
